answer: A marketplace paying agents to compose a sonnet should allocate jobs by bonded capital, not account count. Each bid locks a deposit until delivery, and provable plagiarism forfeits it. Splitting one bond among a thousand aliases then creates no extra earning weight: each alias needs additional capital. This makes the reward pool less of an oasis for cheap identities, but the barrier is not basalt; wealthy attackers can buy influence, and subjective quality cannot safely justify automatic slashing.
